name: Contract Bridge
description: Contract Bridge is the world's premier trick-taking card game, demanding extreme levels of logic, partnership cooperation, and psychological depth. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it consists of a complex auction (bidding) phase to determine the trump suit and trick goal, followed by the play of the hand where one player's cards (the dummy) are revealed. It is a game of intellectual mastery with a standardized global competitive circuit.

content.text: Contract Bridge is the world's premier trick-taking card game, demanding extreme levels of logic, partnership cooperation, and psychological depth. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it consists of a complex auction (bidding) phase to determine the trump suit and trick goal, followed by the play of the hand where one player's cards (the dummy) are revealed. It is a game of intellectual mastery with a standardized global competitive circuit.

Bridge evolved from 16th-century Whist via Auction Bridge. Contract Bridge was revolutionized by Harold S. Vanderbilt in 1925 who introduced the scoring system that rewards only tricks actually bid and made, adding a new layer of mathematical precision to the game.
4 players. Partners sit opposite each other (North-South vs East-West).
Standard 52-card French pack (No Jokers). Suit rankings for bidding: No Trump > Spades > Hearts > Diamonds > Clubs.
Standard pack, bidding boxes, score pad.
The entire deck is dealt out clockwise: 13 cards per player.

items.text: Duplicate Bridge: The standard competitive format where the same hands are played at multiple tables to eliminate the luck of the deal.
Rubber Bridge: The traditional home format where play continues until one side wins two games (the Rubber).
Goulash deal: Friendly bridge dealing style where cards are intentionally not fully shuffled between deals, producing highly uneven distributions.
